subject: openCR: inclusion of mask covariates and derived D.units

messages.author: e14baef37a11434f
messages.subject: openCR: inclusion of mask covariates and derived D.units
parts:
Just starting to run a longterm CR dataset with openCR. Two questions:

1) I don't see any examples in the vignette or the examples.pdf using mask covariates to test phi~ or lambda~mask covariate relationships. I presume this is not possible yet? I tried, like I would do in 'secr' with addCovariates(GBmask, hii_poly) and then specified that variable in the openCR.fit() call: list(lambda~hii, g0~t+b+Trap_Type, sigma~1), but it did not work. Just want to make sure I am not missing something obvious.

2) I am getting an error when I attempt to create derived() parameters:
derived(osecr.t.b.trap)
Total number observed 596
Parameters in model lambda0, phi, lambda, sigma
Error in cat("Superpopulation density", x1$superD * Dscale, D.units, "\n") :
  object 'D.units' not found



Thanks, and excited to see this ML version of open SECR models available.

parts:
OK, I can replicate the #2 error below. But I also provide a fix based on another user’s suggestion.
library(openCR)

####
##Replicate "object 'D.units' not found" error
####
ovenCHr <- rotate(ovenCHp, 90) # rotate for horizontal plot
nets <- traps(ovenCHr)[[1]]
msk <- make.mask(nets, buffer = 300, nx = 50, type = "trapbuffer")
plot(msk)
plot(ovenCHr[[1]], add = TRUE)
plot(nets, tracks = TRUE, add = TRUE)

msk <- make.mask(traps(ovenCHp[[1]]), buffer = 300, nx = 25, type = "trapbuffer")
fitsp <- openCR.fit(ovenCHp, type = 'JSSAsecrlCL', model = lambda0~t, mask = msk)
derived(fitsp)
#Error in cat("Superpopulation density", x1$superD * Dscale, D.units, "\n") : 
#object 'D.units' not found

##but solved, as suggest by another member: by doing
a <-derived(fitsp)
a$estimates



Another issue I am having is using trap covariates. I think I’ve replicated my error here:
####
##Replicate trapcov error
####
for(i in 1:length(session(ovenCHp))){
  covariates(traps(ovenCHp)[[i]])$binom <- rbinom(n=nrow(traps(ovenCHp)[[i]]), prob=0.7, size=1)
  
}
class(ovenCHp) <- class(ovenCHr)

fitsp <- openCR.fit(ovenCHp, type = 'JSSAsecrlCL', model = lambda0~binom, mask = msk)
###Error in openCR.design(capthist, model, type, timecov = timecov, sessioncov = sessioncov,  : 
##covariate(s) binom not found

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: openCR: inclusion of mask covariates and derived D.units
parts:
OK - that isolates the bug to the print method for the derivedopenCR object class output by derived.openCR. You can call the print method directly with explicit Dscale argument, so in theory this should work for bears per 1000 km^2:
print(a, Dscale = 100000)

Note also that derived is now a generic with methods for secr and openCR objects.

On your other point, I would check that the covariate assignment is doing what you think it is. Also start a new thread for a new problem.

messages.subject: Re: openCR: inclusion of mask covariates and derived D.units
parts: In response to 1), would it be appropriate to use an individual covariate to solve this problem? My thinking would be to add habitat covariates such as the mean % forested around each animals centroid as an individual covariate. Animal 1 occupies an area, on average with 10% forest, Animal 2, with 40% forest, and so on. This would be done manually before and added into the capture history.
